revision: R7-07 (B7: global-fetch alias gap closed by an enforceable criterion)
policy: B (FD:L3264): no module calls fetch except HttpTransport. B (FD:L1218, FD:L3263, FD:L4943) import rules stay in dependency-cruiser, unchanged from m1-draft-0.4/annex/dependency-rules.json and m1-draft-0.5/annex/import-and-fetch-rules.json.
previousGap: 0.5 listed `const g = globalThis; g['fe'+'tch'](...)` as NOT flagged and called it a residual. A known bypass cannot pass the policy test; 0.7 replaces the rule with a criterion that has no such bypass.

criterion.C1-static: In every module except src/net/HttpTransport.ts (and a single declared bootstrap file, if any), no free reference to any of these global names: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, Request, importScripts, navigator, globalThis, self, window, frames, parent, top, opener, Reflect, Function, eval. Because the global object can only be named through these identifiers, aliasing it requires a flagged reference: `const g = globalThis` is itself a violation.
criterion.C2-runtime-no-eval: The remaining way to reach the global object without naming it is to construct code at runtime (for example ({}).constructor.constructor('return this')()). MV3 extension pages and the service worker run without 'unsafe-eval' (the default extension CSP), so Function and eval construction throws. Test: in the built extension, evaluate that expression from a non-HttpTransport module under TestHooks; it must throw EvalError.
criterion.C3-runtime-capture: P (optional defence in depth): HttpTransport captures fetch at module evaluation and replaces globalThis.fetch with a throwing, non-configurable stub. Test: after startup, globalThis.fetch() from any other module throws, and HttpTransport still works.
criterion.sufficiency: C1 removes every static path to a network global or to the global object; C2 removes every dynamic path to the global object; together they enforce the policy. C3 is not required for sufficiency.

eslintText: no-restricted-globals: ['error', 'fetch', 'XMLHttpRequest', 'WebSocket', 'EventSource', 'Request', 'importScripts', 'navigator', 'globalThis', 'self', 'window', 'frames', 'parent', 'top', 'opener', 'Reflect', 'Function', 'eval'] for files src/**/*.ts, ignoring src/net/HttpTransport.ts. no-restricted-globals reports every reference to a global variable that is not shadowed by a local binding (the free-reference test of C1).
